A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3DGSim research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V2 reports original rigid-body, elastic, and cloth simulation experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations, and scene-editing demonstrations.

after.justification: V3 retains original simulation experiments and adds Spring-Gaus comparisons, variable-input evaluations, and real-world HO-Cap results.

M1.justification: The original simulator remains, but v3 introduces a substantive real-world adaptation in Section 5.4: pretrained DepthAnything3 replaces MVSplat, a second DPT head predicts latent features, and embedded sparse 3D hand keypoints provide action conditioning. V2 discussed action conditioning only as future work.

E1.justification: V3 adds actual evaluation on HO-Cap real-world hand-object interactions, including single-hand manipulation and bimanual handovers. V2 covers synthetic rigid, elastic, cloth, and edited/multibody scenes. The new MOVI attribution identifies the source of the retained rigid dataset rather than establishing additional coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds Spring-Gaus comparisons on rigid and elastic trajectories and a constant-frame baseline on HO-Cap. CosmosFT also joins the editing and multibody comparisons. The detailed quantitative table drops unfine-tuned Cosmos, although Figure 8 retains it and adds CosmosFT curves.

E3.justification: V3 adds FVD evaluation, variable-length inference tests, and Spring-Gaus fitting/testing on the same trajectories with ground-truth masks and ground height. HO-Cap introduces 15 FPS training and three context cameras without additional target-camera supervision. The reported Cosmos conditioning changes from nine to five frames; this does not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The six original appendix ablation tables survive unchanged as v3 Tables S3-S8. New analyses examine variable-length inference, HO-Cap rollout degradation and failures, and CosmosFT editing/multibody errors. V3 Table 1 labels 18.19 PSNR as 'Without TEM', but retained Table S8 assigns that result to early merging with embeddings, leaving a distinct no-TEM experiment unestablished.

E5.justification: V2 already reports ± values and shaded curves. V3 additionally defines the HO-Cap bands as standard deviations across sequences and explains the averaging in Appendix F.3. Neither version supplies training-seed or repeated-training-run counts.

E6.justification: V3 adds Spring-Gaus, HO-Cap, variable-input, and FVD outcomes. Comparing v2 Figure 11 with v3 Table S1, rigid 4-12 latent future PSNR changes from 28.28 to 28.35, and cloth 4-8 latent from 26.98 to 26.46. Newly reported FVD favors two-step latent models over four-step models across all three synthetic datasets, unlike their future-PSNR ranking.

T1.justification: The Gaussian representation, serialization, temporal encoding/merging, reconstruction objective, and appendix equations retain their mathematical substance. Equations are renumbered or split for presentation. New spatial-causality arguments are conceptual interpretations, without new formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The five principal contribution claims remain intact. V3 reframes the abstract around complementing 2D video generation and adds a conclusion-level claim that spatially grounded interactions ensure realistic dynamics. These refine the positioning and claimed properties without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations for variable-input degradation and real-world failures, substantial Spring-Gaus comparability qualifications, and an image-metric rationale in Appendix E. The discussion introduces a tradeoff between 3D spatial constraints and generative freedom. It also interprets particle penetration and disappearing-hand failures as evidence of learned spatial causality, extending v2's interpretations.

D1.justification: V3 documents the real-world implementation through the DepthAnything3 giant-large-1.1 variant, DPT-head training, hand-keypoint embeddings, and context-camera supervision. It also specifies Spring-Gaus inputs, four-frame velocity initialization, and three evaluated trajectories per object. MOVI provenance is newly disclosed, and reported H100 training time changes from approximately five to six days.

R1.justification: New Appendix D substantially expands the distinction between predictive simulation, dynamic reconstruction, and per-scene analytical simulation, discussing 4DGS, DeformableGS, PhysGaussian, PhysDreamer, and Spring-Gaus. New references also support HO-Cap, DepthAnything3, DINOv3, and other positioning updates. This exceeds bibliographic or citation-style changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, inverse-renderer explanation, benchmarking, generalization, and discussion undergo substantial rewriting. V3 adds a main-text ablation section, moves simulation-speed reporting and detailed benchmark results into the supplement, and reorganizes the appendices into six thematic sections with expanded explanatory prose.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column main layout, removes the original simulator-overview table, and replaces the small main-text results display with an expanded appendix table containing FVD. It adds an ablation summary, CosmosFT curves and comparison panels, and HO-Cap visualizations and metric plots. Existing architecture diagrams and synthetic rollouts are largely retained but relocated or reformatted.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens v2's synthetic-only proof of concept through an implemented action-conditioned HO-Cap adaptation, a documented 3D comparator, and tests exposing input-window and rollout limitations. These address important validation gaps. The gains outweigh the reporting problems, although unequal Spring-Gaus settings, the conflicting TEM ablation label, and stronger causal interpretations limit the conclusions supported by the expanded evidence.
